geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Patty paper: map one triangle onto another with a translate, rotate, reflect.

Goal: I can explain why SAS follows from the definition of congruence.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
SAS: if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to two sides and the included angle of another, the triangles are congruent.

Why, from rigid motions: given AB = DE, AC = DF and angle A = angle D. Translate so A lands on D. Rotate about D so ray AB lies along ray DE; since AB = DE, B lands on E. If C is on the other side of DE from F, reflect across DE. Angle A equals angle D, so ray AC now lies along ray DF, and AC = DF puts C on F. All three vertices match, so a rigid motion maps one triangle onto the other.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: In SAS, why must the angle be the one between the two sides?
slides.reveal: The proof lines up ray AC along ray DF using the angle at the shared vertex A; an angle elsewhere does not control where C lands.
